patch.longFormSummary:
Plant and programme

  • Al Shuaibah 1 is a solar photovoltaic plant in Makkah Province, Saudi Arabia. Its 600 MW plant rating is separate from the combined two-plant programme.

Operation and timeline

  • ACWA’s 2025 prospectus records commercial operation in November 2024. The month is the stated precision, not a verified exact opening day.

Cost and ownership

  • The plants are jointly owned through ACWA Power, Badeel and SAPCO. The combined financing announcement does not publish a plant-specific construction budget; no share of that programme total is assigned here.

Public reaction

  • The owner welcomed the financing milestone as progress toward Saudi renewable-energy goals. This is an attributed programme reaction shared by both plants, not an independent assessment of this plant’s operation.

Contractor reaction

  • Swiss Energy reported starting work with CEEC on the 2.6 GW Al Shuaibah programme in June 2023. This is shared programme context; a separately identified Al Shuaibah 1 rendering remains unavailable.

Construction-support imagery

  • TIMC publishes two equipment photographs for its Al Shuaibah 1 & 2 support contract. They show shared-programme equipment logistics, not separately identified Al Shuaibah 1 buildings or an official plant rendering. Capture dates and the individual plant are not identified.

Reported commercial-operation outlook

  • November 13, 2024 reporting records ACWA’s receipt of a commercial-operation certificate for the full 600 MW Shuaibah 1 project and its expectation of a Q4 2024 financial impact. This attributed company outlook is separate from the earlier financing and contractor statements.

patch.longFormSummary:
Site and development

  • Amazon announced a third northwest Louisiana data-center campus at Resilient Technology Park in Shreveport on August 18, 2026. STACK Infrastructure is the developer and owner; the campus supports cloud computing and AI.

Investment and jobs

  • The additional campus has USD 6 billion of planned investment and 210 expected direct new jobs. The USD 18 billion investment and 750 direct jobs describe all three regional campuses, not this site alone.

Construction and delivery

  • KSLA’s August 18 report gives a first-building completion target in 2027 and a full-project buildout of three to five years. These are reported targets, not completed milestones.

Infrastructure and public process

  • Amazon says it will fund the infrastructure required by its operations. The up-to-USD 400 million water investment covers all three campuses and is not a separate Resilient construction budget.
  • Caddo officials sought water safeguards and environmental impact studies in June. Commissioner John Atkins supported development while calling for impact studies; those requests do not establish that all permits or appeals have been completed.

Public-process photographs

  • The gallery includes KSLA photographs from the December 17, 2025 community meeting and December 18 council debate concerning the west Shreveport data-center proposal. These document public process, not physical construction. December 18 reporting records a 7–0 special-use-permit approval that overturned the planning commission’s denial.

Site context

  • Louisiana Site Selection publishes an undated Resilient Technology Park marketing plan. It is shown as park background only; its lot layout is not represented as the later AWS data-center design, a current approval or a surveyed project boundary. A verified AWS-specific official rendering remains unavailable.

patch.longFormSummary:
DOE’s April 2024 briefing outlined a 250 MWac coal-to-solar demonstration across Nicholas County and Deep Lake sites, with a USD 557 million total project budget and up to USD 129 million federal cost share.

The presentation separates solar from a future 75 MWac battery project. Its Q4 2026–Q3 2028 construction window was a plan, not proof that construction began. Individual site budgets are not allocated here.

Component scope in the DOE planning record

  • DOE’s budget-period-1 determination identifies Nicholas County Solar Project at 100 MWac on approximately 3,400 acres and adjacent Deep Lake Energy Center at 150 MWac. The determination covers planning, design and site characterization; later funding requires further review and authorization. These historical component ratings do not prove current construction, commercial operation or continued funding.
